If you can't wait to get your hands on the latest Apple product on launch day, Apple's refurbished product store has always been a solid option. Typically, you need to wait around three months after a new product launch before the first batch of refurbished units appears on Apple's website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but note that their standards and warranty policies differ......

Apple Certified Refurbished

When you buy from the Apple Certified Refurbished store, you typically get around a 15% discount, and the products are identical to brand-new units. Specifically, Apple guarantees all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing by Apple
  • Brand-new outer shell, so absolutely no scratches or wear
  • Brand-new battery, with the same battery life as a new unit
  • All original accessories and cables included
  • Comes with Apple's standard one-year warranty, same as a new product
  • Also eligible to purchase AppleCare+

Basically, the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed may have more attractive pricing, but note that you won't get the same quality assurance:

  • Inspected and tested by the seller, not Apple
  • Used outer shell, so there will be scratches and wear (see below for details)
  • Used battery, guaranteed to have at least 80% of original capacity only
  • Accessories may not be original Apple products
  • 90-day Amazon warranty, not Apple's one-year warranty

As for scratches and wear, Amazon offers three tiers:

  • Premium / Excellent: No visible cosmetic damage when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Only minor scratches, barely visible when holding the device from 12 inches away
  • Acceptable: Scratches are clearly visible and can also be felt

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is far vaguer than Amazon in describing what you get for your money:

  • No commitment to cosmetic condition, only guaranteed "like-new performance and reliability"
  • Beyond the above, no details mentioned about battery condition
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only get 90 days. The company does not clearly define each tier.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want a product whose appearance and warranty are completely identical to a new one, Apple's refurbished store is clearly the top choice.

However, Amazon Renewed's prices can be much cheaper, and if you're willing to accept the trade-offs mentioned above, it's actually quite a good deal here. Especially if you take our advice and choose to upgrade to the iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's model to save money (you'll only lose out on the (PRODUCT)RED color), there are some truly attractive deals here:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (original price new $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (original price new $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (original price new $1,599) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (original price new $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (original price new $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (original price new $1,299) — Only $1 more than the all-time low

As for Walmart Restored, I'd be concerned that their promises are too vague, but if you're not satisfied, you can indeed opt to return it.
